public_rationale: Both halves hold on 2023 evidence. On arithmetic, the top supercomputer in November 2023 sustained about 1.2 exaflops on Linpack, vastly beyond any human rate. On cognitive flexibility, humans solved about 91% of ConceptARC abstraction tasks in 2023, against 52% for the best program and 25–33% for GPT-4. On planning, the best LLM (GPT-4) produced valid plans in only about 12% of commonsense planning instances in a NeurIPS 2023 study. 'Way behind' is rhetorical, but these gaps are large under any ordinary reading.
limitations: The planning study has no direct human baseline.
Symbolic planners do well on the same domains when given formal models. The claim holds most clearly for flexible planning in novel settings, not for all machine planning.
Benchmarks stand in for broad abilities.

statement.document_title: AI versus The Clumsy Human Mind

from_speaker: Machines are actually already light years ahead of humans
on some variables (like computing floating point arithmetic)

our_interpretation: 'Machines' means the best available computers and AI systems in 2023.
'Light years ahead' on floating point arithmetic means machine speed and accuracy far beyond a human, which plainly holds if machines perform many orders of magnitude more operations per second.

'Way behind' on cognitive flexibility and on long-term planning in unusual situations means leading AI systems scoring well below humans on tests of novel abstraction and of plan generation in unfamiliar settings.
No period is named. I use 2023-01 to the post date of 2023-11-25, the period covered by evaluations of GPT-4-era systems and the November 2023 TOP500 list.

criteria.contradiction_condition: 2023 evidence shows leading AI systems at or near human level on flexible abstraction or novel planning tasks.

evidence.excerpt: Frontier leads the pack with an HPL score of 1.194 EFlop/s – unchanged from the June 2023 list.
evidence.explanation: The top machine sustained about 1.2 quintillion floating point operations per second on the Linpack benchmark, vastly beyond any human rate. This supports 'light years ahead' on floating point arithmetic.

evidence.excerpt: the overall accuracy of humans was 91%, compared to the first-place Kaggle program’s accuracy of 52%, and GPT-4’s accuracy of 25% (using temperature 0.5).
evidence.locator: Section 3 (Previous Evaluation of LLMs using the ConceptARC Benchmark)
evidence.explanation: On tasks that test applying abstract concepts flexibly to new cases, both the best program and GPT-4 were well below humans in 2023. This supports 'way behind' on cognitive flexibility.

evidence.excerpt: However, GPT-4’s performance remains well below the high performance of humans, supporting the conclusion that, even with more informative prompting, the system lacks basic abstract reasoning abilities tested by this corpus.
evidence.explanation: Even with better prompting, GPT-4 reached only 33% in November 2023, so the flexibility gap was not an artefact of weak prompting.

evidence.excerpt: Our findings reveal that LLMs' ability to generate executable plans autonomously is rather limited, with the best model (GPT-4) having an average success rate of ~12% across the domains.
evidence.explanation: The best LLM in 2023 produced valid plans only about 12% of the time on standard planning domains. This supports 'way behind' on planning. The paper also finds better results when external planners and verifiers are added.
